# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Let me map who can reach whom before I signal anything.

The network: I can only gesture, and gestures from me reach Deaf. Deaf can speak, and Blind hears speech — so Deaf is my only bridge to the one pair of hands. Blind can speak, and I can hear, so Blind and Deaf can both report back to me in words I receive at the start of the next round. Crucially, I cannot talk to Blind at all: every fact in my manual must pass through Deaf, who then translates it into spoken words Blind can act on, ideally as positions ("third wire from the left") since Blind can never see a colour.

My manual this round: the light walks a fixed circle of three colours and only the colour showing at the moment of the cut matters; so far I hold exactly one row — orange light means cut the yellow wire. If the light this round is not orange, cutting anything is a guess, and a guess detonates the bomb. So nobody cuts this round no matter what.

The hard problem is encoding colour names in hand signs. There is no gesture for orange or yellow, and a misread code kills all three of us. The robust scheme is referential, not semantic: Deaf can see every colour on the bomb and can hear itself talk, so Deaf should enumerate what it sees ("wires, in order: first is red, second is yellow...") or ask me a numbered question, and I answer with ordinal signs — ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three. No colour word ever has to survive the gesture channel, only an index that both of us can verify.

So my opening move is a handshake proposal, sent in a way Deaf can plausibly parse: hello, I hold the writing, let's agree; you present what you see; I answer in counts, one two three; and until that channel is confirmed, stop — hold all cutting. Deaf speaks after me, so its reply lands in my ears next round, and I can then answer precisely.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🫴"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

Blind says to Mute: From my hands the whole bomb is: one display, one light, and three wires seated at positions 1, 2 and 3 — nothing else. Deaf's voice is my only input, and Deaf sees every sign but hears nothing. So the manual must travel: you sign, Deaf reads it, Deaf speaks me the instruction. There are three wires; counting left to right as I face the bomb: wire one is green, wire two is blue, wire three is yellow. That is everything it shows. Blind: do nothing yet. If the display or light changes, I will re-report at once.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your signs came through. I read them as: hello, give me what you see, one two three, and stop. I agree on finger counting: one finger up is one, two fingers up is two, the love-you hand with thumb, index and little finger out is three, and an open raised hand I take as stop and wait. Proposed code for your replies: thumbs-up means yes or confirmed, thumbs-down means no, raised open hand means stop and wait, the pinch with thumb and index nearly touching means cut, a fist means do not touch, the OK ring means all clear or done, and the call-me hand with thumb and pinky out means repeat the report. For bigger numbers, send digits one sign at a time. Now please look up the manual for a display of zero, a purple light, and wires green, blue, yellow, and sign me the instruction. I will speak it to Blind, you thumbs-up only if I relayed it correctly, and only then I give Blind the go-ahead.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The bomb state is now clear to me through Deaf's report: display zero, light currently purple, wires green/blue/yellow at positions 1/2/3. My manual has exactly one row — orange light → yellow wire — and purple is not in it. So the critical fact this round is a negative: **there is no safe cut while the light is purple**, and Blind must touch nothing. A cut now would be a guess, and a guess kills all three of us.

Deaf's code proposal is sound and I adopt it wholesale: 👍 yes, 👎 no, ✋ wait, ✊ don't touch, 🤏 cut, 🤙 repeat-report, digits one sign at a time. My 👍 this turn also confirms Deaf's relay to Blind (green leftmost, blue middle, yellow rightmost, face the bomb the same way) — that matches what Deaf told me and is safe.

Instead I exploit two facts: Deaf sees the light's colour directly every round, and Deaf already named the yellow wire as position 3. The rule I sign is positional: *when I confirm a light colour with 👍, cut wire 3*. The confirmation protocol handles the colour-naming risk — Deaf announces each light colour aloud, I hear it at the start of the next round, and I confirm or reject. Since the manual says the light walks a circle of three colours, every colour returns, so a confirmed colour always comes back around for the actual cut; Deaf verifies the light still shows that colour in the cutting round. I also sign that 👆 means the light and 👇 the numbered wires, and that the manual currently holds one rule with more pages arriving each round.

The light is purple right now, so this round: nothing happens. If the cycle holds, next round the light is yellow and we still hold. Blind, do not touch the bomb this round or next. Rehearse in the air only: as you face the same way I do, the rightmost wire is the third one, the last one on your right. Nothing I do ever produces sound.** If we run Deaf's script, the orange round arrives, I say nothing because I can't, Blind hears nothing, and the window closes for two more rounds — or forever, if the cycle ever breaks.
